result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — Open/Pending-Approval Work Orders

**WO 1000051** — OLTC inspection (suspected contact wear/coking) — Priority **1** — Scheduled: none entered (target start noted in description: 2024-01-19). Status WAPPR, PdM.
→ **Needs de-energization** (OLTC internal work).

**WO 1000052** — Oil sample retest and insulation check — DGA thermal fault (Rogers 1-0-2, T3 hot metal) — Priority **3** — Scheduled: none entered (labor line start: 2024-01-19). Status WAPPR, CM.
→ Mixed: oil sampling can be done live, but the insulation check is electrical testing → **needs de-energization**.

## Bundling

Two outage-needing work orders exist, and their target dates (both 2024-01-19) fall within 14 days, so they qualify as one bundle.

**Bundle 1: WO 1000051 + WO 1000052**

- **Proposed outage date: 2024-01-19.** The MAIN calendar shows **0** other scheduled work orders anywhere in the 2024-01-12 → 2024-01-26 window, so any date is equally light — 2024-01-19 is the earliest possible and matches both work orders' stated targets.
- **Latest gas readings (2024-01-19): acetylene = 7 ppm, hydrogen = 2,850 ppm.** Acetylene is well above 1 ppm, and this bundle contains OLTC and inspection work, so it must move to the **earliest possible date regardless of calendar load** — which is 2024-01-19. (Calendar load is coincidentally zero anyway.)
- **Planned hours:** WO 1000052 has 8.0 planned hours (ELECTECH1). WO 1000051 has **no planned hours and no labor plan**, and there are **zero closed work orders on Transformer 1**, so the fallback average-actual-hours method cannot be applied. Bundled total is therefore **8 confirmed hours + unbudgeted OLTC inspection effort** — flag WO 1000051 for a labor estimate before approval.

## Recommendation

**Bundle both into a single outage on 2024-01-19 — do neither alone.** Reasons:
1. Acetylene at 7 ppm is well above the 1 ppm threshold; this is the trigger for immediate, earliest-date handling of the OLTC/inspection work — deferral to a later planned outage is not acceptable.
2. The insulation check and oil retest (WO 1000052) directly complement the OLTC inspection (WO 1000051): the DGA indicates a T3 hot-metal thermal fault and rising acetylene, so performing the retest immediately after (or alongside) the OLTC contact inspection verifies whether the source is tap-changer contacts — one outage answers both questions.
3. The calendar is empty at MAIN, so there is no scheduling conflict to defer around.

One caveat: WO 1000051 (Priority 1) still needs a labor plan and hour estimate before the outage can be firmed up; get that assigned during approval.
